- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+10% from prior 10d mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast peak at +10% above prior 10d high.
- If supply_net is negative and bullish sentiment is low (≤0.33), model underestimates; add +3–6% to forecast mean for 30d horizon.
- When official events are frequent (≥20 events/30d) and bearish sentiment dominates, model tends to lag; shift forecast downward by 1–3% relative to prior 10d average.
- For 30d forecasts with high volatility (true outcome std > 5), apply mean reversion: cap forecast at 1.5σ below prior 10d mean if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.33/1.00 alternation), model overfits to recent trend; use 3-period moving average to smooth forecast.
